raw_response:
I farm the way I always have to think about it: first make sure the land gives me steady grain, then leave a little area for cotton to bring cash. I am not farming many mu, and people in my house also work outside, so I cannot make things too complicated. For me, wheat and maize on the same land are still the safest. Everyone around here does that, and even if one side is not so good, at least the family still has grain and some income. I will keep about 10 mu in wheat-maize rotation, and 5 mu in cotton. Cotton takes more watching and picking, but if the price is decent it still helps with cash. I do not dare spend too much on fertilizer at one time, so I will use moderate amounts, mostly like what worked before, and add a little later only if the crop looks weak. Water from the well is useful, but pumping costs money, so I will irrigate at the key stages, not too many times.

For wheat, I will sow in early October with the local improved seed most people buy from the township shop. I usually put base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress once around jointing if the leaves are not dark enough. Wheat cannot be starved too much or yield drops badly, so I would rather spend a bit there. After wheat harvest in June, I will plant summer maize right away on the same 10 mu, because the turnaround is tight and there is no time for fancy tillage. For cotton on the 5 mu, I will keep fertilizer and water moderate. Cotton can make money, but with my labor and age I cannot expand it too much, especially because picking needs hands and hired labor costs a lot.
